refuted.fact: Four substantive rule facts are recorded as what the 2026-05-18 NCUA proposal proposes: 706.103(a) joint licence application; 706.106(a) 120-day decision / deemed approved; 706.107(a)(2) issuance on an open, public or decentralized network is not valid grounds for denial; 706.112 an insured credit union may only invest in an NCUA-licensed PPSI.
refuted.why: This is the biggest finding. The May 18 document says the opposite about its own scope. In Section IV it states verbatim: 'As noted, the NCUA is providing a high-level summary of portions of the NCUA Licensing Proposal to assist stakeholders as they review this NCUA Standards Proposal. Unless explicitly stated in this supplemental proposal, the NCUA is not reproposing or otherwise modifying those provisions proposed in the NCUA Licensing Proposal.' I extracted the full text of the February 12, 2026 proposal PDF (91 FR 6531, doc 2026-02868, RIN 3133-AF69) and confirmed that 706.103, 706.106, 706.107, 706.112, the phrases 'deemed approved', 'open, public, or decentralized' and '120 days after receiving a substantially complete' are ALL already in that February document. They are February provisions, merely restated in May's regulatory text for readability. An article dated 2026-05-18 saying 'NCUA this time proposed a 120-day deemed-approval rule' is wrong about what happened on May 18. What May 18 actually proposed is Subparts B-E (706.201 activities, 706.202 reserve assets, 706.203 redemption, 706.204 risk management, 706.205 audits/reports, 706.3xx custody, 706.4xx capital and operational backstop, 706.5xx AML supervision) plus the share-insurance and tokenized-share amendments.

refuted.fact: '提案 706.106(a)：…收件後 30 天內須通知申請人是否實質完整。' — the 30-day completeness notice attributed to 706.106(a).
refuted.why: 706.106(a) contains only the 120-day decision rule and the deemed-approval consequence. The 30-day notice is 706.106(b)(2): 'Not later than 30 days after receiving an application, the NCUA will notify the Applying Issuer as to whether the NCUA determined the application to be substantially complete.' The cited paragraph number is wrong for that half of the fact.

refuted.fact: '文件末尾署名為「By the National Credit Union Administration Board, this 14th day of May, 2026. Ji Kwon, Acting Secretary of the Board.」'
refuted.why: The quoted string is verbatim correct, but it is not at the end of the document. It sits at line 8,259 of 10,667 in the raw text — the end of the PREAMBLE — immediately followed by 'For the reasons stated in the preamble, the NCUA Board proposes to amend chapter VII of title 12…' and about 2,400 more lines of regulatory text. The document's actual end is '[FR Doc. 2026-09915 Filed 5-15-26; 8:45 am] BILLING CODE 7535-01-P'. Separately, ADDRESSES names 'Melane Conyers-Ausbrooks, Secretary of the Board' while the signature is 'Ji Kwon, Acting Secretary of the Board' — if the article names an office-holder it must use the signature block, not the mailing address.

refuted.fact: '四個主要聯邦支付穩定幣主管機關為 NCUA、FDIC、OCC 與聯準會理事會。'
refuted.why: The source says 'the primary Federal payment stablecoin regulators, WHICH INCLUDE the NCUA, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), and the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System' — 'include', not 'are'. The document nowhere defines the term: I checked all 37 occurrences of 'primary Federal payment stablecoin regulator' in the full text and 706.2 has no definition of it. The article must write 「包括」, not 「就是這四家」.

unsupported.fact: Public Law 119-27 / 139 Stat. 419 / codified at 12 U.S.C. 5901-5916, cited to federalregister.gov/…/2026-06974.txt and …/2026-06963.txt
unsupported.why: I confirmed both footnotes verbatim (FDIC fn 1: 'Public Law 119-27, 139 Stat. 419 (codified at 12 U.S.C. 5901-5916).'; Treasury/OFAC/FinCEN fn 1: 'GENIUS Act, Public Law 119-27, 139 Stat. 419 (2025) (codified at 12 U.S.C. 5901-5916).'). But neither URL is in sources[], so a reader of the finished article cannot trace it. And the NCUA document itself never says 'Public Law 119-27', never says '139 Stat.' and never says '5901-5916' — I grepped the full text and got zero hits for all three; it only ever writes '12 U.S.C. 5901 et seq.'. Re-source to the statute at govinfo.gov/content/pkg/PLAW-119publ27/html/PLAW-119publ27.htm, whose NOTE tags run 12 USC 5901 through 12 USC 5916 and which ends 'Approved July 18, 2025.'

unsupported.fact: govinfo public-law metadata (Law Number, Date Approved, Bill Number, Full Title, Legislative History) cited to govinfo.gov/wssearch/getContentDetail?packageId=PLAW-119publ27
unsupported.why: That is an undocumented internal JSON endpoint, not a citable page, and it is not in sources[]. The data is correct, but the fact must be re-pointed at sources[2] (govinfo.gov/app/details/PLAW-119publ27), which I confirmed carries every one of those fields server-rendered in its HTML. Also, the package id PLAW-119publ27 is a formulaic construction built from a public-law number the researcher took from another agency's footnote; if it was assembled rather than searched for, that is exactly the pattern the BRIEF forbids, even though it resolves.

The source string is 'CONGRESSIONAL RECORD, Vol. 171 (2025): May 21, June 2, 9, 11, 12, 17, considered and passed Senate.' Those are the dates on which the Record shows the bill being CONSIDERED; the Senate passed it once, not on six separate dates. As worded the fact asserts six Senate passages, which the source does not say.

The NCUA document's footnote 13 cites only '12 U.S.C. 5902(b)(1)'. The section-3 mapping is derivable from footnote 42 ('section 3(d) of the GENIUS Act (12 U.S.C. 5902(d))') but is never stated for (b)(1) on the cited page. I verified independently from the statute that SEC. 3 carries NOTE 12 USC 5902, so the mapping is TRUE — but it needs the statute URL attached rather than the NCUA full-text URL. The researcher also dropped the second half of footnote 13, which materially changes the picture: the parallel prohibition on offering stablecoins issued by non-compliant FOREIGN issuers takes effect on the GENIUS Act's effective date, not in 2028.

unsupported.fact: 'NCUA 理事會於 2026 年 5 月 14 日通過'
unsupported.why: The document gives an authorization/signature date ('By the National Credit Union Administration Board, this 14th day of May, 2026'), the standard Federal Register attestation line. It does not say a Board meeting was held or a vote taken that day, and records no vote tally. Write '文件署名日為 5 月 14 日' or '理事會於 5 月 14 日授權發布', not '通過'.

unsupported.fact: The four-prong definition of 'Subsidiary of an Insured Credit Union' including the all-tiers catch-all
unsupported.why: Prong (4) ('A subsidiary of any entity that meets the definition of a Subsidiary of an Insured Credit Union. All tiers or levels … are included') is genuinely in the proposed regulatory text of 706.2, so it is verifiable. But the same document's preamble says 'This definition includes three separate prongs' and lists only (A)(B)(C), footnoted to 12 U.S.C. 5901(33). The article must separate the three statutory prongs from the NCUA's proposed fourth all-tiers prong, or it will read as if the statute has four.

unsupported.fact: comments_close_on = 2026-07-17 presented as the single, unambiguous comment deadline
unsupported.why: Correct against the FR DATES field and the NCUA press release, both of which say July 17, 2026. But the same API response's regulations.gov docket block gives comment_start_date 2026-05-18 and comment_end_date 2026-07-18 for NCUA-2026-1024-0001. Use the rule's DATES field and do not also cite regulations.gov for the deadline.

additional_findings: MISSING AND MATERIAL FOR THIS VERTICAL — proposed 706.201(c)(3) forbids an NCUA-licensed PPSI from marketing or representing that Payment Stablecoins 'are backed by the full faith and credit of the United States, guaranteed by the United States Government, or subject to Federal deposit insurance or Federal share insurance.' The preamble says the same: 'The GENIUS Act explicitly dictates that Payment Stablecoins are not backed by the full faith and credit of the United States, they are not guaranteed by the U.S. Government, nor are they covered by deposit or share insurance from the FDIC or NCUA.' A crypto-vertical article that omits this omits the single most reader-relevant protection fact in the document.

MISSING — proposed 706.201(c)(4) prohibits paying a holder 'any form of interest or yield (whether in cash, tokens, or other consideration) solely in connection with the holding, use, or retention of such Payment Stablecoin', with a rebuttable presumption covering affiliate and related-third-party arrangements (706.201(c)(4)(i)-(iii)). The preamble ties it to section 4(a)(11) of the GENIUS Act and the rulemaking authority in section 4(h). This is a regulatory prohibition, so it sits inside crypto.md's line, and it is the answer to the obvious reader question about yield.

MISSING — proposed 706.201(c)(7) forbids providing a customer credit, directly or indirectly, to enable that customer to buy Payment Stablecoins from the issuer; 706.201(c)(5) forbids pledging, rehypothecating or reusing required Reserve Assets except in three named cases.

MISSING — proposed 706.203(b)(1)(i): the required redemption timeframe 'may not exceed two business days following the date of the requested redemption', and 706.203(a)(2) requires a statement that discretionary limits on timely redemption can only be imposed by the NCUA.

MISSING — proposed 706.401(a)(1): a de novo NCUA-licensed PPSI must hold minimum capital equal to the greater of its licensing-condition amount or $5 million, for 36 months (de novo = licensed within the prior 3 years). 706.401(b): an operational backstop equal to 12 months of total expenses, held only in US coin and currency / Federal Reserve balances, demand deposits or share accounts fully insured by the FDIC or NCUA, or US Treasuries with 93 days or less remaining maturity, separately identified from reserve assets.

MISSING — tokenized shares, which is where this document actually breaks new ground and the clearest thing it offers a general reader: 'a FICU member or accountholder using tokenized shares is afforded the same Federal share insurance coverage under the FCU Act as a FICU member or accountholder using non-tokenized shares', and the proposal would amend the share-insurance regulations to codify that the technology or recordkeeping used does not affect whether a liability is an insurable 'account'. The contrast — tokenized shares ARE share-insured, payment stablecoins are NOT — is the article's natural spine.
MISSING — the document asks 199 numbered questions for comment (Question 1 through Question 199), which conveys that this is a consultation and not a settled rule.

MISSING AND NEWSWORTHY — the statutory rulemaking deadline. GENIUS Act SEC. 13 (NOTE: 12 USC 5913): 'Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, each primary Federal payment stablecoin regulator, the Secretary of the Treasury, and each State payment stablecoin regulator shall promulgate regulations to carry out this Act through appropriate notice and comment rulemaking.' Enactment 2025-07-18, so the deadline was 2026-07-18. I queried the FR API for conditions[term]=stablecoin over 2026-01-01..2026-09-16 (44 documents) and every GENIUS Act implementing document from NCUA, OCC, FDIC, FinCEN/OFAC and Treasury is still type 'Proposed Rule' — no final rule from any regulator as of the check date. SOURCE THIS TO THE STATUTE, NOT THE NCUA DOCUMENT: the NCUA full text contains zero occurrences of '1 year', 'one year after', 'July 18, 2026' or 'not later than 1 year'.

TRAP — do not compute the GENIUS Act's effective date. The NCUA document states only the rule ('the earlier of 18 months after the enactment date (July 18, 2025) or 120 days after the primary Federal payment stablecoin regulators issue final regulations'). The string '2027' appears ZERO times in the entire 634,750-byte full text. Writing '2027年1月18日生效' would be the article's own arithmetic. If it is wanted, cite GENIUS Act SEC. 20 (12 USC 5901 note) from the statute and still present it as a formula, since prong (2) can pull the date earlier.

BETTER FIRST-PARTY SOURCE — https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/PLAW-119publ27/html/PLAW-119publ27.htm (HTTP 200, 185,846 bytes) is the complete enrolled text of the GENIUS Act: SEC. 3 (12 USC 5902) with the 3-years-after-enactment prohibition, SEC. 13 (12 USC 5913) rulemaking deadline, SEC. 20 (12 USC 5901 note) effective date, 'Approved July 18, 2025.' and the same legislative history. It should replace or accompany the /app/details/ metadata page as sources[2], because every statutory fact in this article currently leans on a second agency's footnote instead of on the statute.

BETTER FIRST-PARTY SOURCE for the February proposal — https://ncua.gov/newsroom/press-release/2026/ncua-proposes-rule-permitted-payment-stablecoin-issuer-applications (HTTP 200) is the NCUA's own announcement of the Licensing Proposal, 'Alexandria, VA (February 11, 2026)', comment close 'April 13, 2026', with Chairman Hauptman saying 'This proposed rule is the first step in NCUA's implementation of the GENIUS Act' and 'We're on track to meet the Congress' July 18 deadline.' Both are vendor claims and must be attributed; the second gives no year, so it cannot by itself support a 2026-07-18 deadline.

DATE PRECISION — the NCUA press release's 'available for review' hyperlink points to https://www.federalregister.gov/public-inspection/2026-09915/… , i.e. the PUBLIC INSPECTION copy. The correct three-step chain is: Board signature 2026-05-14; filed with the Office of the Federal Register and placed on public inspection, with the press release issued, 2026-05-15 08:45; published in the Federal Register 2026-05-18. Saying the rule 'was in the Federal Register on May 15' conflates public inspection with publication.

TERMINOLOGY MISMATCH to handle explicitly — the Federal Register ACTION field says 'Supplemental proposed rule.' while the NCUA's own press release calls it 'a Notice of Proposed Rule Making'. The supplemental also carries a DIFFERENT RIN (3133-AG10) from the February Licensing Proposal (3133-AF69), and a different docket, even though it supplements it.

CROSS-CHECK CONTEXT not recorded, all first-party — from the NCUA footnotes: Treasury ANPRM 90 FR 45159 (Sept. 19, 2025); Treasury NPRM 90 FR 59409 (Dec. 19, 2025); NCUA Licensing Proposal 91 FR 6531 (Feb. 12, 2026); OCC 91 FR 10202 (Mar. 2, 2026). From my own FR API search: FDIC 91 FR 6138 (Feb. 11, 2026) and 91 FR 18534 (Apr. 10, 2026); OFAC/FinCEN 91 FR 18582 (Apr. 10, 2026, action 'Joint proposed rule.', agencies Treasury + OFAC + FinCEN — the researcher's labelling of 2026-06963 is correct); Treasury 91 FR 53368 (Aug. 18, 2026).

STATUS RE-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY — I queried the FR API for all NCUA documents published 2026-05-18 through 2026-09-16: exactly 25 documents, of which the only Proposed Rules are 2026-09915 (this one) and 2026-10817 'Regulation for Federal Financial Assistance'. No final rule, no comment-period extension, no correction. The researcher's status finding holds. The API also reports 37 comments filed on NCUA-2026-1024-0001 and regulations_dot_gov_open_for_comment: false.

SOURCING HYGIENE IS OTHERWISE CLEAN — all four sources[] entries are first-party (GPO/govinfo, NCUA newsroom); none is a news outlet, aggregator, law-firm blog or search snippet; the Hauptman quotes are correctly flagged is_vendor_claim: true and are verbatim correct against the live page, including the original's mismatched straight/curly quotation marks. The researcher's reported byte counts (634,750 bytes / 10,667 lines for the full text; 581,110 bytes for the PDF) match mine exactly, so they did fetch what they said they fetched.
